title: Twitch is using your content to train Amazons AI. Heres how to opt out.
body: Creating content on Twitch ? Unless you've changed your settings, it's being used to train AI . Twitch creators recently spotted a "Training for Generative AI" setting in account security that's toggled on by default. "Allow your channel content to train generative AI content models at Amazon," the description reads. Needless to say, people weren't happy . SEE ALSO: Twitch's CEO says passive scrolling can't beat the community of live streaming Digging in to Amazon-owned Twitch's FAQs reveals a bit more information on what, exactly, this means. "Generative AI content models are AI tools that can help create or synthesize content outputs like text or images when given instructions or prompts because they are also trained on content," reads the FAQ . "When you allow training, that means that your content may be used for future Gen AI model improvements. An example of what happens when you allow your content to be used for training a GenAI content model is that your audio might help refine models that create speech to text, which would help improve captions at Twitch but would also help improve captions across Amazon." Addressing the backlash during a livestream on Wednesday, Twitch's chief product officer Mike Minton gave a slightly revealing answer to the question of why the option was switched on by defaul. Well, there s an honest answer, Minton said, per Kotaku . And I think most of you probably can appreciate this: If it was opt-in, nobody would opt-in. Um, that s honestly the answer. title: Netflixs Raygun doc trailer looks to breakdance through the viral storm
body: It's been two years since Australian Olympic breakdancer Rachael "Raygun" Gunn gained international attention with her kangaroo-hopping performance at the 2024 Paris Olympics . Now, Netflix 's upcoming documentary Untold Raygun: Breaking Badly gives Gunn a platform to address critics and chronicle going viral after her maligned, highly-memed routine won zero points from Olympic judges . Almost overnight, the breakdancer became the subject of a wave of online hate , while accusations were made around Gunn's rise to the Olympic stage. "There was this frenzy. It was a growing monster," Gunn says in the trailer. "Some of the memes were funny. Then the tone started to change." Judging by the comments on Netflix's YouTube video , such speculation is far from over. It remains to be seen how Untold Raygun: Breaking Badly , directed by Chapman Way and Maclain Way, will handle such matters. Untold Raygun: Breaking Badly is streaming on Netflix Sept. 1. title: The Perseid meteor shower peaks this week: Heres how to see it
body: Throughout most of July and the start of August, the Perseid meteor shower has been lighting up our skies. The annual celestial event is known for being one of the biggest meteor showers of the year and is a highlight many stargazing calendars. While it's been happening for the better part of a month, the peak dates are coming up this week. So, if you want to catch a glimpse of some meteors shooting across the sky, here's everything you need to know. When will the Perseid meteor shower peak? The Perseids have been active since July 17 and will run until Aug. 24. The peak dates are Aug. 12 13, according to NASA . What is the Perseid meteor shower? According to NASA , the Perseids occur when Earth passes through debris left behind by comet 109P/Swift-Tuttle . As tiny pieces of rock and dust hit our atmosphere at high speeds, they burn up and create the bright streaks visible in the night sky. The Perseids can also produce fireballs, or bright flashes caused by larger pieces of comet debris. How to see the Perseid meteor shower For the best chance of catching the Perseids, NASA suggests watching the sky from midnight through to the early morning hours. Find somewhere as dark as possible, away from streetlights and other sources of light, and give your eyes a little time to adjust once you're outside. There s also some good news for this year s display: the Perseids peak falls close to the New Moon, so bright moonlight shouldn t wash out the fainter meteors.

title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on August 13
body: We're now into a new lunar cycle, but it'll take a few more nights before the Moon becomes easy to spot again as it gradually grows brighter. What is today s Moon phase? As of Thursday, Aug. 13, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon phase is in Waxing Crescent phase, with 0% of its surface visible. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on August 28. What are Moon phases? The Moon doesn't look the same from Earth every night. As it travels around our planet, it moves through a lunar cycle that takes roughly 29.5 days to complete, according to NASA . The changing positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon affect how much of the Moon's sunlit side we can see, creating the different phases. Over the course of the cycle, the Moon progresses from a narrow crescent to a half Moon and eventually a Full Moon, before starting the sequence over again. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it s not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible. Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere) Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit. title: ICE agents could soon use gloves that give painful electric shocks
body: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers could soon use gloves that can give a painful electric shock to anyone they touch. As first reported by the Associated Press , the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) published a notice on Monday revealing plans to distribute electrically powered shock gloves to ICE agents by the end of March next year. Called the G.L.O.V.E. (an acronym for Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter), the device is developed by Kentucky company Compliant Technologies , which markets it as a "Conductive Distraction and De-escalation Device" or CD3. "CD3s are not weapons they deliver small, non-injurious electrical pulses directly to the surface of the skin, the body s largest and most conductive organ, achieving NPI (Neuro Peripheral Interference)," Compliant Technologies states on its website . In short, the gloves cause a painful electric shock . View this post on Instagram According to Compliant Technologies, the G.L.O.V.E "delivers a pain stimulus strictly to the area" of the skin that it touches, overstimulating and disrupting signals in the nervous system. This overwhelms and overloads the brain, causing a person to instinctively attempt to retreat. "Because the effect is so intense, it disrupts normal thought processes and interferes with expected reactions," the company states. "In most cases, this results in the subject effectively complying or conceding in order to end the effects." title: Toddler's tragic death from brain-destroying amoeba offers lessons for doctors
author: Beth Mole
body: A healthy toddler in Washington state fell ill abruptly. It began with vomiting, lethargy, and weakness on his right side. Then it progressed to a headache, fever, and trouble swallowing. At one point, he briefly became unresponsive, and he had episodes where he stopped breathing. Doctors admitted him to the hospital, but his condition only deteriorated. The boy was infected with an ultra-rare amoeba known for ravaging the brain. The opportunistic pathogen was first identified in 1986 from the brain of a San Diego Zoo monkey, which died from the infection. Since then, only about 200 human cases have been recorded worldwide. About 90 percent of them have been fatal. The initial symptoms can be vague and, given its rarity, the infection is notorious for being undiagnosed or misdiagnosed. Still, the scant medical literature does provide some telltale signs, clues of what it can look like on tests and scans. But for the toddler, the infection looked different, sending doctors down the wrong path. Read full article Comments

title: The web’s newest weapon against AI scrapers is a font
author: Kyle Orland
body: AI companies' penchant for scraping through large swathes of the public web in search of valuable training data has already led to lawsuits and technical fixes aimed at stopping the practice. Now, a pair of designers are hoping to stymie these scrapers with a new font designed to offer people a perfectly readable webpage while serving scrapers a subtly edited, nonsensical version in the underlying HTML. ShieldFont, as designers Isaque Seneda and Gabriel Abrucio write in a recent white paper , was made to offer web publishers "a practical opt-out from unauthorized AI training and [to] disrupt what is collected when that choice is ignored." When is a horse a potato? The font is based around ligatures , a long-standing feature of many fonts that is usually used to replace certain letter pairs with a more readable version when they're smushed up next to each other. With ShieldFont, though, those ligatures are instead used to replace entire words with others in an attempt to destroy the text's value to scrapers. This substitution only happens when the font engine draws the page on screen, meaning scrapers that simply download plaintext source code get an altered version that end users never see. title: Terabytes of credentials leaked in massive supply-chain attack
author: Dan Goodin
body: Terabytes worth of credentials, many belonging to the world’s biggest and most sensitive organizations, have been exposed in a supply-chain attack on LiteLLM, an open source tool that streamlines AI-driven software development. Microsoft, Amazon, Cisco, Samsung, and Salesforce are only a handful of the entities whose access secrets were exposed. The revelation was posted on Tuesday and Wednesday by security firms CloudSEK and Hudson Rock. CloudSEK said it found cloud keys, repository tokens, SSH keys, Kubernetes secrets, package publishing credentials, environment variables, and AI provider keys that could allow attackers to gain access to more than 2,500 organizations. 40 minutes is all it takes The credentials were extracted during a 40-minute window in March while the victims used compromised versions of LiteLLM downloaded from the package’s official location in the Python Package Index repository. Hudson Rock said it made the discovery after analyzing a 195TB file that it obtained. Neither firm identified the source of the information. Read full article Comments

title: Have physicists finally discovered glueballs? New evidence points to yes.
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: Physicists with the Beijing Spectrometer III (BES III) experiment have uncovered convincing new evidence of the existence of so-called glueballs , an elusive composite particle made entirely of gluons predicted by quantum theory. The results appeared in a preprint posted to arXiv last month and were also presented last week at the International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP). All the stuff we see around us is made up of quarks held together by gluons (carriers of the nuclear strong force) to form protons and neutrons, which comprise the core of every single atom. The Higgs boson , discovered in 2012 after decades of searching, was widely touted as the final missing piece of the Standard Model of Particle Physics. But there are still plenty of unanswered questions, including whether or not glueballs really exist. They should, if the Standard Model is correct; they're a direct prediction of quantum chromodynamics, i.e., the theory of the strong nuclear force. There should even be several kinds of glueballs. The launch follows a limited test that began in June. Meta describes the new iPhone app as an " AI-powered daily companion for Facebook creators ." Its pitch boils down to three tasks: mapping out a creator s daily priorities, offering personalized tips to grow, and helping them reply to fans with AI. The app is now available on iOS to Facebook creators in the United States and Canada. An Android version is expected later. What can creators expect from Creator Studio? Creator Studio is designed as an integrated workspace for people who manage their accounts through Facebook but inevitably get pulled into Reels, messages, and the feed. When creators open the app, they see a list of daily priorities, which might include reviewing a recent post, checking progress toward a goal, or responding to comments. At the center of the app is Facebook s AI creator assistant , which the company first introduced in June. The assistant draws from a creator s content, performance, audience engagement, and stated goals to offer personalized recommendations. body: In the first half of 2026, customers spent $50.3 billion globally on TikTok Shop, according to a report by Tabcut and Momentum Works a whopping 92 percent increase over the same period last year. But, as What's Trending reported, the data might be more complicated than it looks. In a May 2026 Harris Poll, 63 percent of Gen Zers said they stopped buying from TikTok Shop . EMARKETER, which published the data, stated that it might be because of increasing dissatisfaction with the marketplace itself. Still, 62 percent said they use TikTok to discover new products, and users ages 25 to 44 are the platform's most active shoppers. As Mashable reported in Nov. 2025, TikTok Shop was reportedly inundated with 70 million sketchy products , partly due to AI. This year, a gray market of GLP-1 drugs is reportedly growing on the platform. The pullback amongst young adults could also be due to other factors like no-buy movements. It could also be due to the economy though, maybe scrolling TikTok Shop and buying a little treat because you can't buy a house is a recession indicator .

title: US boosts drone surveillance as flesh-eating screwworms spread in Texas
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: Hundreds of US government drones have switched from border surveillance to a different surveillance mission this summer—looking for signs of screwworm infestations in wild animals and livestock herds. The flesh-eating New World Screwworm is the parasitic larva that emerges from eggs laid by flies in the open wounds or body openings of warm-blooded animals and humans, with untreated cases potentially leading to severe injury or death. Since the first screwworm cases were detected in South Texas in June, the US Department of Agriculture and US Customs and Border Protection have been conducting “one of the most extensive animal-health surveillance operations in the country,” according to the USDA in social media posts on platforms like X and Facebook on August 10. The effort involves at least 200 drones owned by the Department of Homeland Security, which includes the Customs and Border Protection (CBP) agency. The USDA has described performing more than 1,000 drone flights and surveying more than 22,000 animals so far. Read full article Comments

title: Yes, we saw the video. Heres how to clean your Ninja Creami.
body: Yes, I've seen the Ninja Creami video. On Aug. 11, 25-year-old influencer Arriella Simons posted an update on the Ninja Creami she bought less than two weeks prior. While enjoying her latest Ninja Creami dessert, she found an unexpected mix-in in her ice cream maggots. The source appears to be the lid of Simons' Creami, where maggots have now taken home. If there's ever a video to de-influence you to buy something, this seems to be it, as 8.5 million people have now seen Simons' maggot nightmare. Users like Kailey Rousonelos are in the comments saying, "Welp, being broke has saved me yet again 😭😂." As someone who has tested and highly endorsed the Ninja Creami , obviously, this caught my eye. Turns out, Simons isn't alone in this, as there's a two-year-old Reddit forum with another Creami user posting the same issue. This is not a case of faulty Ninja Creami makers, but a cleaning and maintenance issue. The lid of the Ninja Creami's outer bowl appears to be the culprit. This lid holds the blade attachment and has quite a few crevices that can hold water. And since flies breed in dark, moist areas... well, that's how you end up with maggots. If you want to make sure your Creami stays maggot-free, you have to be cleaning it correctly. How to clean your Ninja Creami The best way to protect against maggots is to properly wash your Creami. title: The FCC banned foreign routers, drones, robots: What it means for you
body: Do you know where the robots running your home your Google Nest devices, AI-powered smart assistants, and, especially, your robovacuums come from? Do you even care? Well, the American government certainly wants you to. In a sweeping order from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) two weeks ago, the Trump administration effectively banned foreign-made "robotic devices" from the U.S. market, including those helpful housekeepers. SEE ALSO: What to look for in a robot vacuum: A guide from someone who tests new vacuums every month The ruling expands the FCC's list of restricted devices under presumed national security concerns, also known as the Covered List . Citing national security concerns, the agency blocked imports and domestic sales of internet-connected devices that navigate independently (like humanoid robots) or carry cameras and microphones (like those terrifying robo dogs ). But these traits also apply to the oft-AI-powered vacuum-mop hybrids that roll around your house when you're not home some of them can even livestream now. Fortunately, the government won't be knocking down doors and sweeping up Roombas anytime soon devices already in circulation can remain in homes across the country, and pre-approved robots can stay on the market. But it has cast uncertainty on the future of new models and the average consumer's access to them. Here's what you need to know if you're in the market for a high-tech cleaner. title: OpenAI employees can apparently complain directly to Sam Altman
body: OpenAI employees apparently have a quick way to reach founder and CEO Sam Altman , Fortune reported. It's an e mail address, friction@openai.com , and its purpose is to give employees a place to report company problems that OpenAI's leadership team can triage and handle. SEE ALSO: What is OpenAI Astra? Everything we know about the new and possibly dangerous new model The friction@ inbox has existed for a while, according to Fortune , but its use widened when Fidji Simo joined OpenAI as CEO of Applications in the fall of 2025. Simo went on a "listening tour" to better understand problems across the company, and formalized the friction@ process. She assigned Irina Kofman, VP of strategic initiatives and operations, to monitor the inbox and ensure that issues were resolved. Simo also established a monthly, company-wide Slack update to track progress, Fortune reported. Simo has since left OpenAI, but these processes remain. One former OpenAI employee told Fortune that the system gives leadership an effective way to hear employee feedback. "It's a good thing literally anybody can complain about big company bullsh*t directly to Sam, and they can act on it," the former employee told Fortune . Examples Fortune reported include a pilot program to prioritize parking spots for workers with longer commutes to combat full lots, and a more reliable process for granting API credits. However, a problem brought to friction@ only gets resolved if Altman and OpenAI President Greg Brockman consider it "worthy," another former employee, who led a team at the company, told Fortune . title: Brennan Lee Mulligan returns with Dimension 20: Toylight trailer
body: Dimension 20 is the tabletop roleplaying game series that just keeps giving. Already in 2026, Brennan Lee Mulligan's actual play show has offered Dropout subscribers Gladlands and City Council of Darkness . Now, this fall comes Toylight. The first trailer for Dimension 20: Toylight promises that this season will reteam Mulligan with his Intrepid Heroes: Emily Axford, Ally Beardsley, Brian Murphy, Zac Oyama, Siobhan Thompson, and Lou Wilson. SEE ALSO: The Dropout lineup that is redefining modern entertainment These improv comedians have created a cast of characters who are all playthings. Murph is Ol' Clyde Horsey, who seems to be a rocking horse who uses his rails as a bow and arrow. Axford is Cutie Pie, a kewpie doll with a Brooklyn accent. Wilson plays Wyon, a battle axe-wielding lion plushie. Oyama is Tinsley, a toy soldier, while Thompson plays a cracked porcelain doll, and Beardsley is a fluffy bunny named Calypso. Sounds cute, right? Well, leave it to the cast that turned Candyland meets Game of Thrones into the most gutting season ( Crown of Candy ) to make Toy Story turned tragi-comedy. Here's the logline for the new season : Dimension 20: Toylight follows a band of toys as they rise up to defend the enchanted Toylight, the last flicker of a dying child's imagination. It's giving Bing Bong. So brace yourselves for being turned inside out emotionally. Dimension 20: Toylight premieres on Dropout on Sept. 16. title: Google brings ASL-to-text translation to Pixel 11
body: Talking to your phone has long been a convenient alternative to typing. With the Pixel 11, Google is extending that option to people who communicate through American Sign Language (ASL). Ahead of its Made by Google event Wednesday evening, Google DeepMind announced SL2T, a new AI model that translates sign language directly into written text. The model powers a sign-to-text feature launching in Gboard and Live Transcribe on the Pixel 11 family. In practice, the feature allows users to use sign language via their phone s camera for tasks they would typically use keys to perform. That could mean signing a Google search, drafting a text or email, writing in a document, or asking Gemini a question. In Live Transcribe, a user can sign a response during an in-person conversation instead of typing it out. The feature initially translates ASL into English. Google says it will come to more devices soon, at no additional cost, with support for additional sign languages planned for the future. SEE ALSO: Made By Google: Live updates as new Pixel 11 phones launch How does sign-to-text work? Teaching a phone to understand sign language takes more than showing it a dictionary of hand gestures. ASL is its own language, with distinct grammar and meaning conveyed through movements of the hands, arms, torso, head, and face, sometimes all at once. That means SL2T has to pay attention to the signer s entire upper body. An on-device computer vision system tracks 130 points across the person s face, body, and hands, essentially turning the video into a moving map of geometric coordinates. The raw

title: Two hydrogen-burning engines powered this car to a new land speed record
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: It's been far too long since I've been able to report a new land speed record. For a while, it looked like Bloodhound might have been able to make good on its 1,000 mph (1,609 km/h) attempt, but then the money ran out . As a result, Thrust SSC's two-way average of 763.6 mph (1,229 km/h), set in 1997, remains the fastest anyone has ever driven a wheeled vehicle over a timed mile . But yesterday, on the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah, a new record was set by the JCB Hydromax for hydrogen-powered cars. JCB is a UK-based manufacturer of heavy industrial and agricultural equipment—think diggers, loaders, backhoes, tractors, and so on. And as JCB is based in the UK, it doesn't have the luxury of being able to ignore carbon emissions targets; it has to have alternatives to diesel engines. For some products, that means switching to batteries, but the company has also been working with hydrogen. At first, that meant fuel cells, but after developing prototypes, JCB concluded the tech was too expensive and too fragile for life on the farm or the construction site. Instead, in 2020, the company started developing its own hydrogen combustion engine. The idea of burning hydrogen in an internal combustion engine has been tried before with little success. For example, in 2006, BMW modified a naturally aspirated V12 engine in a 7 Series to run on hydrogen, which it did, but with 60 percent of the power and five times the fuel consumption compared to gasoline. body: The Trump administration is trying to stop New York from enforcing its gambling laws against Kalshi, and yesterday said it ordered the prediction market to continue operating in the state. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) announced that it exercised its emergency authority in response to a "market emergency." The CFTC said it acted "to ensure market stability" and "ordered the exchange to continue to operate in accordance with the Commodity Exchange Act’s Core Principles." The Trump administration took the action after a request from Kalshi. The market emergency alleged by the CFTC is that New York Attorney General Letitia James sued Kalshi on July 31. James' lawsuit seeks a court order to permanently enjoin Kalshi "from operating an unlawful gambling business" in the state. title: The Wrong Girls review: Kristen Stewart and Alia Shawkat shine in stoner buddy comedy
body: Following in the footsteps of Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar and Romy and Michele's High School Reunion, writer/director Dylan Meyer's The Wrong Girls is a sublimely stupid buddy comedy. And thank the movie gods! When it comes to male-fronted buddy comedies, there's no shortage of cinema celebrating loyalty alongside the giddy pleasure of acting really, truly idiotic with your friends. Beyond movies like the Cornetto Trilogy, practically every Kevin Smith movie, or any Will Ferrell comedy, there are also several franchises in this vein, sparked by Dumb and Dumber , Bill Ted ' s Excellent Adventure , and Wayne's World. Female-fronted buddy comedies are fewer and farther between in general, and even more so when it comes to movies that allow the actresses at their center to truly embrace their inner bozo. Sure, in Clueless and Bridesmaids, the heroines make silly mistakes. But they're ultimately relatable and even enviable figures, thanks to their coveted wardrobes, flawless beauty, and dream-guy-secured happy endings. Cheers then to Meyer, who, for her directorial debut, looked at celebrated actresses Alia Shawkat and Kristen Stewart (Meyer's real-life wife), and saw what terrific dum-dums they could be. The Wrong Girls embraces dirtbag girlhood. Kristen Stewart and Alia Shawkat co-star in "The Wrong Girls." Credit: NEON Stewart and Shawkat star as Frankie and Molly, two best friends who share a home, two cats, a bong, and an utter lack of ambition. title: Booksellers suspect AI firms are buying and then destroying rare books
author: Ashley Belanger
body: If you can truly appreciate an old book—and maybe even marvel at how its fragile, yellowing pages contain some of the earliest ways that people tried to make sense of the world around them—then headlines about tech companies destroying books to train AI likely torture a tender part of your soul. It’s indeed depressing to imagine piles of book spines waiting to be fed into wood chippers while torn-out pages are cropped, scanned, and trashed. But that’s the cheapest and easiest way to scan books as fast as possible, and AI companies are in a race to advance their models by training on the kind of engaging, high-quality, long-form texts that can only be found in books. So book lovers fear it’s likely that the practice is happening on a grander scale than is currently being reported and that some physical copies of books will be lost forever. What makes this destruction extra painful, though, is that it doesn’t have to be this way. Read full article Comments

title: New space object masquerades as a star the size of our solar system
body: Astronomers have found the earliest example of a black hole rapidly bulking up in the universe and it may finally resolve a long‑running cosmic dilemma. The object appears just 660 million years after the Big Bang . Using NASA 's James Webb Space Telescope , researchers found that almost all of its light comes from a central black hole wrapped in a tight shell of stormy hydrogen gas, rather than from stars in a surrounding galaxy. SEE ALSO: Solar Eclipse 2026 livestreams: How to watch safely today without glasses That alone is striking. But what really matters is the clarity of the signal. After using computers to simulate different possibilities, the team was able to rule out stars and dust as the main sources of its incredible light. That makes this object, dubbed MoM-BH*‑1, the strongest evidence yet of a newly proposed type of space object a so-called black hole star giving scientists a firm blueprint for a whole population of puzzling objects Webb has spotted near the beginning of time. "You have something that looks a bit like a star but is 100 billion times brighter," said Rohan Naidu, lead author of the study and an MIT fellow at the time, in a statement. "That means you can't be powering this by nuclear fusion, which is the energy source that sits at the heart of all the stars we have." The object is mind‑boggling: a black hole that is about 100,000 times more massive than the sun , sitting at the center of an enormous ball of gas. title: The End of Oak Street review: Imagine Jurassic Park but bleak and stupid
body: What if Steven Spielberg were a misanthrope? On its surface, The End of Oak Street plays like a pastiche of Spielberg work, cherry-picking elements from Jaws and Jurassic Park, including signature moments of sound design and score. Yet the question at its core is not really about whether its American nuclear family will survive. (It's a Hollywood summer movie, after all.) It's what happens when the Amblin aesthetic is used as a husk to express a deep disdain for humankind. Warner Bros. gave writer-director David Robert Mitchell (It Follows) a blockbuster budget that enabled top-notch visual effects and A-list stars like Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor. And in return, he gave the studio a survival action movie bursting with ferocious feathered dinosaurs, but also oozing with existential dread and a slyly regressive politics. On its surface, The End of Oak Street looks like summer fun. But it is, in fact, as bleak and infuriating as the recent and alarmingly similar Netflix release The Last House. The End of Oak Street is a gory and mean sci-fi adventure. title: Meet the Pixel Tag, Googles answer to the Apple AirTag
body: Google 's version of the AirTag is coming: The Google Pixel Tag. The Google Pixel Tag uses Google's Find Hub network to help you find your belongings, like your wallet or suitcase. It can be used with Android devices running Android 9 or newer; connect it to your device, name it, and even share it with up to 10 people. SEE ALSO: How to watch Made By Google 2026 You can see your tagged items on the map within the Find Hub app. If you lose something, you can ring it if it's within Bluetooth range, and it'll play a sound through its built-in speaker. Apparently, it'll have precise location data thanks to Ultra-Wideband with Bluetooth Channel Sounding, so you can recover your item even if it's in a nook or cranny. Credit: Ren Ramos / Mashable And if you leave your keys or wallet (or pet?) behind, or are about to, you'll get an alert. You'll also get an alert if an unknown tag is with you. Should your tagged item be out of range, Find Hub will tap into a network of over one billion Android devices to find it, according to Google's press release. Credit: Ren Ramos / Mashable The Google Pixel Tag is made of stainless steel and has a battery life of up to one year (which is similar to the AirTag ). At under two inches long, 0.2 inches thick, and weighing 0.4 ounces, it won't add bulk to your valuables. It retails for $29 for one or $99 for a 4-pack. It releases on Nov. 11.

title: Researchers found a way to hijack devices through Zoom screen sharing
author: Lily Hay Newman, wired.com
body: As AI models gain advanced capabilities to find vulnerabilities in software, develop ways to exploit them , and even carry out autonomous hacking sprees , researchers offered a sobering new example on Tuesday, disclosing vulnerabilities in the video conferencing platform Zoom that could have been exploited to take over targets’ devices. Anyone on a call that involved screen sharing, whether participants or the host, would have been vulnerable to a silent attack that could be carried out with no indication and no interaction from the victim. Researchers from the digital defense firm A Security say the bug was discovered in early June using publicly available AI models, and that it took fewer than 20 prompts to uncover the vulnerabilities and create a working attack. Zoom issued a security advisory on Tuesday, including details about fixes the company has already begun rolling out to address the flaws, which affected devices running all operating systems that Zoom supports—Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android. “What is interesting for us and what we believe is dangerous is the democratization of these capabilities—the barrier to entry is dropping rapidly,” A Security cofounder Omer Gull told WIRED ahead of the disclosure. “Before it would have taken a team of five people maybe six months with a lot of refining and iteration to find this. Now people can reach the same results with under 20 prompts. And Zoom is an important type of target because people assume trust when using it. They don’t see it as a threat.” Read full article Comments

title: Formula E finds a new home on Disney+, ESPN+
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: Formula E is set to make a big change in terms of visibility when season 12 gets underway this December. It has signed a new multiyear deal to broadcast the sport on Disney+ and ESPN+ in 144 countries, with live coverage of each entire ePrix, from practice through qualifying to the race. The new media deal means that here in the US, Formula E will be shown on ESPN+ from next season; since 2023, the sport has been shown live on Roku. "This is a landmark moment for Formula E and reflects the incredible momentum behind our Championship," said Formula E's CEO Jeff Dodds. "Disney’s unrivaled global reach and storytelling will introduce Formula E to millions of new fans while bringing them closer than ever to the drama, innovation, and excitement of electric racing. As we enter the GEN4 era, this provides an exceptional platform to accelerate our global growth and continue building one of the world’s most exciting sports properties." Actually, the new deal will mean fewer eyeballs on the sport, at least here in the US. More than 100 million US households subscribe to Roku (as of April this year), whereas ESPN+ has been losing subscribers since peaking at the end of 2023 and is now down to roughly 24 million households in the US. title: My favorite dating app just released *another* safety feature

But that level of sauciness isn't for everyone and to be fair, Pure isn't the only place you'll find randos sending you unsolicited photos of their unruly trunks among the forest. If you're a Woman on the Internet and you've used a dating app , you may have (unfortunately) received an unsolicited explicit photo, which is known as cyberflashing . For women ages 18 to 49, that number jumps to 56 percent. So, Pure one of the most sex-positive dating apps I've ever tested is stepping up to stop cyberflashing with a brand-new feature called My Media Rules. The tool lets you set your own universal boundaries for the app, meaning you can choose to auto-block all nude pics, turn off media sharing completely, or keep things open. You can even toggle these permissions on a chat-by-chat basis. Plus, if a graphic image appears for the first time, Pure prompts you to adjust your filters right then and there and lets you decide whether you want to keep talking to the person who sent it. title: Did poop enable the evolution of complex animals?
author: Kiona N. Smith
body: The Cambrian explosion may have been fueled by poop. The first animals on Earth emerged about 600 million years ago, and 60 million years later, those simple early animals evolved into wildly different directions, branching out into a diverse menagerie of complicated new forms and conquering new ecological niches. Known as the Cambrian Explosion, this flurry of rapid evolution produced most of the animal phyla and ecosystems we see around us today. And it may have taken off because some of those early animals evolved a bizarre new ability: pooping. According to a recent study, the first poo pellets helped spread nutrients to deeper parts of the ocean, fueling the evolution of bigger animals in more diverse ecosystems. title: This map shows how many Flock cameras are in your neighborhood
body: Flock cameras are swiftly becoming the bane of citizens' existence , with the U.S.-wide network of automated license plate readers (ALPRs) increasingly coming under public scrutiny . Now, there's an app that can show you how many devices owned by surveillance company Flock Safety are in your neighbourhood. Reported by the New York Times , DeFlock Maps is a crowdsourced app aiming for "surveillance transparency " that pinpoints ALPRs including Flocks on a map. SEE ALSO: What are Flock cameras and why are they so controversial? The map uses crowdsourced data from contributors to DeFlock and is powered by open-source project OpenStreetMap . According to the app's website, "Camera locations come from volunteers and the OpenStreetMap community, not a private company or government agency." Devices pinned include not just Flock cameras but those of Motorola Solutions, Genetec, and other unnamed tech companies. However, Flock cameras make up over 80 percent of the devices mapped. "Mass surveillance infrastructure is expanding rapidly in our communities, often without public awareness or consent," DeFlock's user guide reads . "DeFlock makes surveillance infrastructure visible. By documenting these devices and uploading the data to OpenStreetMap, we create a transparent, searchable record of the surveillance apparatus in our communities. Knowledge is power, and transparency is the first step toward accountability." While the annual Perseids will deliver one of the year's most popular meteor displays, the solar eclipse will offer a different kind of spectacle as the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun. While parts of Europe will experience a full show in the form of a total solar eclipse, those based in North America will still have a chance to catch the celestial event as a partial eclipse. Keep reading to find out all you need to know about this latest celestial event. When is the solar eclipse in North America? On Aug. 12, a partial solar eclipse will be visible across parts of North America and most of Canada. On Aug. 12, the moon will sweep its shadow across the top of the world, briefly turning day into twilight along a narrow path through Greenland, Iceland, northern Russia, northern Spain, and a sliver of Portugal. That's the path of totality where the sun is completely blocked and it's the first time in 27 years that mainland Europe has gotten a full, real-deal solar eclipse. But people in the United States won't be in that bullseye. Instead, a part of the country will see a partial solar eclipse, where the moon nips the sun but never covers it completely. The sky won't go dark, the stars won't pop out, and you won't get the full moody effect . But with the right eyewear, you could still see the sun turn into a yummy space crescent roll in the middle of a Wednesday. Originally created by engineer Josh Wardle as a gift for his partner, Wordle rapidly spread to become an international phenomenon, with thousands of people around the globe playing every day. Alternate Wordle versions created by fans also sprang up, including battle royale Squabble , music identification game Heardle , and variations like Dordle and Quordle that make you guess multiple words at once . title: Chrome adopts what may be the best protection yet against account takeovers
author: Dan Goodin
body: Google’s Chrome browser has added a new feature that could go a long way in preventing a form of account takeover that’s grown increasingly common as users adopt two-factor authentication, passkeys, and similar protections. The new Chrome protection is known as device-bound session credentials (DBSCs). The measure stores a unique encryption key in a silicon-resident fortress that’s built into the device running the browser. On Windows machines, this fortress is called a TPM, short for Trusted Platform Module. On macOS and iOS, it’s known as a secure enclave. Other platforms have differing names. Recently released versions of Chrome for Windows and macOS generate a key that’s stored in this fortress. An antidote to session cookie theft DBSCs protect against the theft of session cookies, the unique strings of characters that websites store on browsers. Session cookies greatly speed up browsing on sensitive sites that require user authentication. Instead of requiring the exchange of credentials each time a user opens a new site page, the server sets a session cookie that effectively proves the user has already successfully logged in. title: iOS 27 beta 5 arrives. Here’s what’s new.
body: The latest beta release for the iPhone 's operating system, iOS 27 beta 5, is here. With this release from Apple come some design changes and feature updates. However, new features and design tweaks aren't the biggest news to come with this new beta release. iOS 27 beta 5 provides references to 6 unreleased iPhone models, essentially confirming the upcoming iPhone 18 lineup for the very first time. What's new with iOS 27 beta 5? The most visual updates with iOS 27 beta 5 are new icons for several major Apple apps. Safari, Siri, Preview, App Store and Remote app icons have all received updates. Some other apps have received more minor Liquid Glass-related tweaks. Siri's AI update continues to receive upgrades as well. iOS 27 beta 5 brings more voice customization options. Pace and Expressivity can now be adjusted for all of the available American English voices and the British English voices as well. Contacts also received a slight upgrade. If a company is associated with a specific contact, Contacts will now show that company name under the contact's name and in the search results. Apple is providing users with more control over the Search function on their iPhone in iOS 27 beta 5. Users can choose whether app results appear in Search. If turned on, users can also control whether Search results show four or eight apps. There's a new "Search the Web" option at the bottom of Search results too. body: Google has been all-in with Gemini for the last several years, and despite some animosity online, the bet is paying off. CEO Sundar Pichai announced today that Gemini has reached 1 billion monthly active users (MAUs), an important milestone for any Google product. While 13 other Google products have managed that feat, Gemini has done it faster than any other. Gemini has wormed its way into virtually every Google product and service, powering email organization in Gmail, document summary in Drive, and much more. Gemini is also core to Google's flagship search experience, with AI Mode and AI Overviews becoming increasingly hard to avoid. The 1 billion-user metric has nothing to do with any of that, though. These 1 billion users may also be encountering Gemini in all those places, but that's not the MAU metric. Pichai is talking only about people who are opening the Gemini app or visiting the Gemini web interface to enter a prompt or access Gemini Live. As the memory chip shortage rages on, a new report from the Taiwanese newspaper United Daily News (UDN) says PCs are facing further price hikes as Microsoft raises its Windows 11 licensing fees for device manufacturers. According to a PC brand executive who spoke anonymously to UDN, Microsoft normally bumps its Windows license fees for PC makers by small margins every year. However, the latest increases are much higher than usual. SEE ALSO: RAMageddon is making it harder to find the best Windows laptops. These 10 are actually worth it. "In the past, licensing fees mostly increased by single digits each year, but starting in July this year, the average increase has reached 7 percent to 10 percent," UDN wrote. Other brand executives interviewed by the newspaper noted that the licensing fee increases vary by processor type; more powerful devices with higher-end CPUs have seen bigger increases than lower-end models. These licensing fee changes are already impacting current PC prices, per UDN's sources. That would make sense since most Windows laptops and desktops sold to consumers come with their operating systems pre-installed. (In a win for DIYers, pricing for individual Windows 11 licenses remains unchanged.) When reached for comment by Mashable, a representative for Microsoft said the company "has nothing to share at this time." title: Used EV buying guide: The $30,000 edition
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: A strange thing is happening in the used EV market. Supply is up thanks to an ever-increasing stream of ex-lease cars reaching the market, and yet prices have been going up as well. As a result of America's latest war in the Middle East, used EVs have appreciated by just over 5 percent since February. Despite the stronger pricing, used EV sales have been strong this year—up 25 percent year over year by May, although a weaker June has brought overall sales up just over 20 percent year over year, according to the analysts at Cox Automotive. Used EVs also hang around on dealer lots a lot less than new ones—the same analysts at Cox found just 38 days' supply of used EVs in June, but 81 days for new EVs. And much of the demand is at the cheaper end of the spectrum, say the analysts at Recurrent . In previous installments of our used EV buyers' guide, we've already looked at the most affordable used EVs, ending last time at $25,000 —EVs that may now qualify for a $1,750 rebate if you're in California. Today we're looking at used EVs that cost between $25,000 and $30,000, and according to Autotrader's search, there are more than 9,000 used EVs for sale in that price range. Broadly, you can split the results into three buckets: Cars where you'll find plenty to choose from; ones where there might be a couple of hundred for sale nationwide; and then the oddities where there might just be a handful to pick from. title: Spotify will now tell you when an artist isn’t real
body: That new singer in your Spotify playlist may have a name, a face, and a carefully written bio. Soon, Spotify may also tell you the person they describe doesn t exist. Beginning in mid-September, the streaming platform will place an "AI Persona" badge on profiles built around AI-generated identities. Music from those profiles will also be excluded from Spotify s editorial playlists and algorithmic recommendations by default, the company announced Aug. 11. Spotify will stop introducing listeners to AI Personas by default. Their songs should no longer pop up in Discover Weekly, Release Radar, or another personalized playlist unless you have already shown interest in the artist. You can still search for, play, and follow them, and following one may tell Spotify that you re open to hearing more. Put simply, the company doesn t want an AI Persona to be something you discover by accident. Credit: Spotify That is also the frustration Spotify says it has heard from listeners, who "don t like seeing an artist profile that seems human, only to find out that the persona is AI-generated," according to the announcement. The data suggest plenty of listeners share that concern. As Mashable reported in 2025 , 97 percent of respondents could not distinguish a fully AI-generated song from one made by humans. Still, 80 percent wanted AI music clearly labeled, and 72 percent wanted to know if a streaming service was recommending it. title: Less than 2.5% of Taylor Farms' recalled lettuce went to Taco Bells
author: Beth Mole
body: Though shredded iceberg lettuce at Taco Bell restaurants has been a prime suspect in an explosive outbreak of the diarrheal parasite Cyclospora , a new report from the Food and Drug Administration finally reveals where all the contaminated lettuce was sold—and only a tiny sliver of it went to Taco Bell locations. The feces-tainted lettuce was sourced from Mexico and sold by Taylor Farms, a mammoth produce provider based in California. Taylor Farms has drawn scrutiny for its ties to the Trump administration and reluctance to provide information amid the outbreak, which has now sickened over 23,000 people across 47 states, killing two and sending over 500 others to the hospital. Taylor Farms reportedly attempted to delay issuing a recall amid the illnesses and, since then, has refused to clearly report how much tainted lettuce it recalled and where all of it had been shipped. The FDA's Enforcement Report finally provides some answers: Taylor Farms recalled a total of 236,192 cases of lettuce due to potential Cyclospora contamination. Of those, only 5,900—just shy of 2.5 percent—were sold to Yum, the parent company of Taco Bell, Pizza Hut, and KFC. The other 97.5 percent of the lettuce that potentially sickened Americans was distributed elsewhere. Read full article Comments

title: Tracking extreme heat by the hour makes climate change seem even worse
author: Scott K. Johnson
body: Global warming is leading to more extremely hot weather. There is perhaps no more obvious consequence of climate change. But changing how we analyze this problem can still help scientists think about it in a different way that may yield surprises. Generally, studies on heat extremes work with some combination of daily minimum, maximum, and mean temperatures. Sometimes they focus on multi-day heatwaves using those metrics, since the discomfort and health impacts increase for longer events. There are different thresholds you can use to define extreme heat in these analyses, either based on past statistics or on the human body’s physiological limits. A new study led by Weilin Liao and Xuanzong Zhang at Sun Yat-sen University tried breaking down heat extremes to the hourly level instead, which reveals some interesting nuances. title: A Google insider spills the tea on how the company forsook its founding ideals
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: In 2018, 20,000 Google employees worldwide made headlines when they staged a walkout to protest how the company had handled sexual misconduct allegations against key corporate executives, among other grievances. One of the organizers was Claire Stapleton , a communications specialist whose distinctive voice and ability to channel the corporate ethos had once earned her the internal moniker "Bard of Google." Six months later, a disillusioned Stapleton resigned, claiming she had been demoted during the most recent restructuring as retaliation for helping to spearhead the walkout. The story of how she went from enthusiastic cheerleader to proactive dissident, and the many lessons she learned along the way, are featured in her new book, Don't Be Evil: Bad Bosses, Fake Promises, and My Escape from Big Tech—A Biting Memoir of Twelve Years Inside Google . Stapleton didn't set out to be a rabble-rouser. When she joined Google out of college in 2007, it was like "getting the golden ticket in Willy Wonka ," she told Ars. Awareness of her good fortune offset any initial uneasiness or skepticism, although Stapleton was sufficiently independent-minded not to move into what was then Google's new corporate housing development in Mountain View, California. Stapleton was very good at her job, and she quickly moved up the ranks, playing a key role in shaping the company's public image. Read full article Comments

title: Trump to give Republicans a 3-1 FCC majority, isn't filling empty Democratic seat
author: Jon Brodkin
body: The Federal Communications Commission has been shorthanded throughout President Trump's second term, but it's about to get a new commissioner. Unsurprisingly, Trump is breaking a historical norm with a nomination that would give Republicans a 3-1 advantage on the FCC. Historically, the president and Senate worked together to ensure that the president's party maintained only a one-vote majority. Normally, the president's party has three FCC members while the minority party has two. Instead of the typical 3-2 split, the FCC has operated with a 2-1 Republican majority during Trump's second term. On Friday, Trump nominated Republican Danielle Thumann Severs to take one of the empty spots. Thumann Severs, a lawyer, has been working as FCC Chairman Brendan Carr's senior counsel. She must be confirmed by the Republican-controlled Senate before being sworn in as a commissioner. Read full article Comments

title: Gentle Monster trailer sees Léa Seydoux facing dark home truths
body: Something's very off in the trailer for Gentle Monster , with L a Seydoux starring as a woman facing dark truths in her own home. And though the film's absolutely not about the Korean eyewear brand , the director was inspired by the company's name . Written and directed by Marie Kreutzer, the film follows concert pianist Lucy (Seydoux) whose idyllic home life with her husband Philip (Laurence Rupp) and son is shattered when the police show up with a search warrant, accusing Phillip of a heinous crime. Forced to reckon with the accusations against the person she loves, Lucy has more than one lie to untangle, and her son to protect. It's a complicated film, thematically, for Kreutzer, whose 2022 film Corsage starred actor Florian Teichtmeister, who was charged for similar crimes. The director told The Hollywood Reporter in May 2026, "In the middle of that whole scandal and shit storm, I thought maybe I cannot make Gentle Monster anymore, because everyone will always make that connection. It didn t take me very long until to realize that I might have to make it even more." From the trailer, we get a glimpse of director of photography Judith Kaufmann's cinematography, music by Camille, and a powerful performance from Seydoux, who stars alongside Jella Haase and Catherine Deneuve. Gentle Monster will premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) in September, before its release in select cinemas Oct. 30. The film will then be streaming on Netflix from Nov. 18. title: New surveillance tech links your phone to your license plate
author: Nicole M. Bennett, The Conversation
body: Imagine that you share a ride to work with the same colleague most mornings. As it passes by a license plate reader, the camera records the car, which can be linked through vehicle records to its registered owner. Beside it, another sensor detects signals broadcast by devices traveling nearby, such as your phone and your colleague’s smartwatch. After enough trips, software may treat some of those devices as a recurring electronic signature associated with the vehicle. Weeks later, one of the same device signals appears alongside a different car connected to an investigation. The signal itself may not contain its owner’s name, but its previous association with a known vehicle gives investigators another clue they can use to work out who was carrying the device. SignalTrace , a system marketed by the security company Leonardo , is designed to work alongside automatic license plate readers. The company says it can recognize groups of consumer devices that regularly move together, then associate them with license plate records and time-stamped locations. The pattern can then be searched even when a police investigator does not know the plate number. Read full article Comments

title: Why Bumble now allows men to message first
body: As of today, anyone can send the first message on Bumble . It's a total rewrite for the dating app where "women make the first move." Another change is also here: Instead of having 24 hours for the message recipient to respond to that first message, they now have 72 hours. SEE ALSO: Men will soon be able to message first on Bumble This update is happening because of user insights and feedback, according to a press release shared with Mashable. Nearly two-thirds (66 percent) of women surveyed by the app say they actually prefer men to send the first message, according to a survey of over 2,200 women on Bumble in the U.S. in Aug. 2024. Many said it'd make dating feel less pressured. Gen Z women said women making the first move remains "an empowering option," but also appreciate the flexibility of men starting the conversation, in research commissioned by Bumble between Feb. and March 2025, of 2,000 singles aged 18-35 who were actively using dating apps. That research also found that nearly two-thirds of both men and women say they feel more confident when they have a choice of when and how a conversation begins. title: New Pass-ta-key attack reveals all the things we didn't know about passkeys
author: Dan Goodin
body: Last week a researcher outlined what he said was a “novel attack surface” in passkeys, the new authentication paradigm that offers a more secure alternative over password-based methods. In fact, the attacks demonstrated in the post are neither novel nor unique to passkeys. This distinction is important because the research has generated confusion among end users and security professionals as they assess whether this new mechanism is truly safe to use. The attack is called Pass-ta-key—a blending of the word passkey with the phrase “pass the key” and a nod to a plate of pasta. Arie Olshtein, a researcher at security firm Palo Alto Networks, described in a post last week how Pass-ta-key could obtain all passkeys stored in the Google Password Manager app (GPM) for Windows when it’s running on a machine infected with malware. This came as a surprise to many people because they believed passkeys are stored exclusively in the trusted platform manager (TPM), the locked-down enclave in a hardened silicon chip that’s reserved for storing cryptographic keys and other highly sensitive information on Windows machines. If passkeys are stored in the TPM, then how was Pass-ta-key able to extract the entire set of passkeys stored by the app, they wanted to know. Read full article Comments

title: Tesla shows first Cybercab with built-in Starlink. Elon Musk explains why it needs one.
body: Tesla 's Cybercabs now come with built-in Starlink connectivity. On Monday, the company's Robotaxi account on X shared photos of the first Cybercab with an integrated Starlink antenna. Check it out up close in the photo below. It fits nicely. But is it needed? Credit: Tesla Given that Starlink is best suited for remote areas where there's no 5G connectivity, and Cybercabs will almost certainly first start operating in dense urban areas , why do Tesla's autonomous taxis even need Starlink? Cybercabs have 5G chips built-in, and the Starlink antenna adds additional cost, weight, and complexity which doesn't appear necessary right now. Tesla CEO Elon Musk has the answer, and it's definitely, absolutely, certainly not so that Tesla can foot another bill to Musk-owned SpaceX . In a tweet , he referenced Cloudflare's assessment that "bot traffic will exceed human (internet) traffic by a factor of 1,000 within five years." This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. "And the only system that can support the insanely fast bandwidth growth needed by AI is Starlink," wrote Musk in a reply. Ever since SpaceX's monster IPO in June, there's been talk about SpaceX and Tesla merging into one giant corporation that covers transportation, energy, AI, chipmaking, and AI compute, both on Earth and in space. Musk himself said there's "more and more overlap" between the two companies, but there's also the question of control. title: Rare Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt variant discovered, to auction this week
body: Almost 100 rare Nintendo cartridges have been discovered in a Wisconsin retro games store, with a handful of them to go up for auction this week. The individually wrapped Super Mario Bros ./ Duck Hunt NES cartridges appear to have come from a previously unknown run of the games, with collectors having been unaware of their existence until now. SEE ALSO: 'The Super Mario Galaxy Movie' review: Death is coming for us all The 97 Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt cartridges belong to Kevin Braun, owner of retro games store OneStopWonders in Waukesha, Wisconsin, and were identified with the help of Nintendo Wire editor Jason Ganos. Nintendo Wire reports that the cartridges were initially in the possession of a precious metal recovery service, which Nintendo appeared to have contracted to break them down. They were left untouched for decades, until Braun purchased the box of games from the owner's grandson. He had been intending to sell the games at OneStopWonders, but forgot them in a storage unit until they came up in conversation with Ganos. "After Kevin finished his story, I immediately could tell that the blood had drained from my face," Ganos wrote, recounting the discovery on Nintendo Wire. Super Mario Bros. and Duck Hunt aren't rare games in and of themselves. Released in the U.S. alongside the NES' 1985 launch, Super Mario Bros. and Duck Hunt have left enduring legacies as two of the platform's most popular titles. In 1988, the games were put together in dual cartridges and sold with the NES in an Action Set bundle. However, Braun's cartridges do not appear to be from this run.

title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on August 11
body: We're almost at the end of the Moon's current lunar cycle, with only the tiniest sliver surface still visible. That crescent will to shrink nothing over the next few nights before the Moon reaches its New Moon phase. What is today s Moon phase? As of Tuesday, Aug. 11, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon phase is in Waning Crescent phase, with 3% of its surface visible. The Moon is not illuminated enough to be able to spot anything on its surface tonight. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on August 28. What are Moon phases? The Moon doesn't look the same from Earth every night. As it travels around our planet, it moves through a lunar cycle that takes roughly 29.5 days to complete, according to NASA . The changing positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon affect how much of the Moon's sunlit side we can see, creating the different phases. Over the course of the cycle, the Moon progresses from a narrow crescent to a half Moon and eventually a Full Moon, before starting the sequence over again. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it s not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible. Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere) T

author: Beth Mole
body: President Trump signed an executive order Monday that makes sweeping, unilateral changes to federal vaccine recommendations. The order aims to reduce the number of lifesaving vaccines all children are recommended to get—from 18 to 11—while also splitting them up and spacing them out over more time and more medical visits. The vaccine changes are not backed by evidence or spurred by new findings. Rather, they are based on false anti-vaccine fearmongering about harms, including the debunked claim that they cause autism, and misinformation that multiple vaccinations can "overwhelm" children's immune systems. This false claim has also been repeatedly debunked and explained . During a signing event at the White House on Monday afternoon, Trump falsely claimed that pediatricians "have a vaccination that looks like the size of a bottle of soda," that is "poured into a little child's body, and bad things happen in too many cases. title: Amazon backs power plant that may become top source of US climate pollution
author: Ashley Belanger
body: Amazon’s artificial intelligence ambitions will soon be partly fueled by a natural gas-burning power plant in Texas that “could become the largest single source of climate pollution in the United States,” The New York Times reported . These gas-burning plants are increasingly lumped into data center projects. They produce harmful pollutants, which can accelerate climate change impacts and harm public health—contributing to conditions like asthma, heart disease, lung cancer, and strokes. Some communities are demanding more stringent environmental reviews, but the Trump administration favors fast-tracking that can include skipping the permitting process entirely. Since Elon Musk’s xAI controversially began relying on gas turbines last spring to power its biggest AI data center, Colossus, there has been public backlash to off-the-grid data centers like the one Amazon is building. body: Social media scuttlebutt about Mark Zuckerberg’s $300 million superyacht failing to assist stranded boaters off the coast of Alaska was partly corroborated by ship-tracking data—and eventually prompted responses from both the US Coast Guard and a spokesperson for Zuckerberg. The incident was made public when Michael Love, a passenger aboard the replica steamship Wilderness Legacy during an Alaska cruise, posted about it on the social media platform Bluesky. The ship detoured to rescue a stranded 21-foot skiff with two women, a child and a dog, after the US Coast Guard had supposedly first radioed Zuckerberg’s superyacht, Launchpad , for help without success. “There was near unanimous booing when the captain announced this,” Love wrote in describing the Alaska cruise passengers’ response to the lack of help from Zuckerberg’s ship.
